newsitem.title: PERU: Fujimori falls in poll as hostage crisis drags on.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori falls in poll as hostage crisis drags on.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's popularity continued falling in March due partly to the length of the Lima hostage crisis that has now dragged on for more than 100 days, a poll showed on Friday.

The survey by pollster Imasen, published in the financial daily Gestion, said approval for Fujimori's management of the country fell during March by 6.1 percentage points to 48 percent. It said 47 percent of those polled disapproved of Fujimori compared with 41.7 percent at the beginning of March.

The paper did not give a margin of error or say how many people were surveyed. It quoted Imasen as saying Fujimori's approval rating also was off due to persistent structural problems in the Peruvian economy.

On the decline through most of 1996, Fujimori enjoyed a surge in popularity in the weeks after about 20 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels seized the Japanese ambassador's home on Dec. 17, taking hundreds of hostages.

But Imasen and other pollsters recorded a renewed fall in early February and that trend has continued. The latest poll, taken between March 21 and 23, found that approval for his handling of the longest hostage siege in Latin America's history also fell in March -- down 6.5 percentage points to 56.5 percent.

The survey said 32.7 percent of those polled feel the government caused peace talks in the crisis to stall during March while 24.9 percent say the MRTA is at fault and 41.6 percent blame both sides. Face-to-face negotiations -- on hold since March 12 -- are expected to restart early next week.

The hostage-takers initially demanded release of about 450 imprisoned rebels but have since said they could negotiate a reduced number as long as those freed were high-ranking MRTA members. Fujimori has rejected their demand.
